response:
It sounds really exhausting to have these thoughts constantly intruding on your life, and it's completely understandable that you want to break free from them. What you're describing—persistent, distressing thoughts that interfere with daily life—is more common than you might think, and you don't have to face it alone.

Consider reaching out to a mental health professional, such as a therapist trained in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), which can be very effective for persistent intrusive thoughts. They can help you develop personalized strategies to challenge and reframe these thought patterns. In the meantime, when the thoughts arise, try gently acknowledging them without judgment and then redirecting your attention to what you're doing in the present moment—grounding techniques like focusing on your senses can help. Small steps toward activities you enjoy, even when the thoughts are present, can also gradually help reduce their grip. You deserve to live fully, and support is available to help you get there.
